newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Most UN Council members support Boutros-Ghali.
newsitem.headline: Most UN Council members support Boutros-Ghali.

text.p: The Security Council began closed-door consultations Monday on nominating a secretary-general, with U.S. ambassador Madeleine Albright under instructions to block a second term for Boutros Boutros-Ghali.
One council member said during a recess that almost all his colleagues, except Albright, had backed Boutros-Ghali's candidacy.

But Britain, while expressing support for the incumbent secretary-general, said the situation had changed in view of the U.S. stance, while Italy spoke of some sort of compromise term instead of the usual five years, he said.

Boutros-Ghali's current term expires on December 31. Albright's spokesman, James Rubin, told reporters: "She has received written instructions from Washington to oppose Boutros-Ghali's candidacy should it be put forward...during the course of today or tomorrow."
Monday's consultations were largely to determine whether there had been any change on the part of the United States, which for months has called for new leadership to reform the world body.

Boutros-Ghali was formally nominated last week by Egyptian U.N. envoy Nabil Elaraby. He also has the backing of the Organisation of African Unity, the Arab League and many other U.N. members, including a large portion of the 15-nation Security Council.
